scope: India: central-government auction of telecom access spectrum by the Department of Telecommunications, 2010 to 2024 - every auction round with spectrum offered, spectrum sold, reserve value, winning bid value, bidders, rounds and per-operator allocation - plus the end-to-end documentary record of the 2G licences issued in 2008, from the CAG's presumptive-value estimates through the Supreme Court's 2012 cancellation to the CBI special court's 2017 acquittal of every accused. Descriptive only. No allegation of wrongdoing against any named company or individual is made or implied anywhere in this file.
readThisFirst: This file's central statistic is the share of offered spectrum that actually sold, auction by auction. It ranges from 100 per cent (2010 3G and 2010 BWA, where DoT records that every block sold) to 1.34 per cent (2024, measured against the 10,522.35 MHz that DoT's own opening release says was put up). The 2016 auction - the one usually described as the failure - sold 964.80 of 2,354.75 MHz, or 40.97 per cent, and that figure is reconciled here from two independent official documents. COVERAGE LIMIT: the 2013, 2014 and 2015 auctions carry partial records; no single official table listing offered-versus-sold for all auctions 2010-2024 was found, so every share in this file is computed from per-auction sources with their denominators published alongside. A HIGH UNSOLD SHARE IS NOT EVIDENCE OF ANYTHING ON ITS OWN: it is exactly what an aggressive reserve price produces, and TRAI's own reserve prices are the other half of every one of these ratios. Nothing in this file establishes why any block went unsold.
method: Per-auction retrieval from the publisher of record: DoT press notes, DoT Notices Inviting Applications, DoT daily and final public auction reports, PIB releases of the Ministry of Communications and of the Cabinet, TRAI recommendations, and the CAG's tabled audit report. Where a figure is computed rather than published - notably the 2016 winning-bid total and the 2012 offered quantum - the arithmetic is stated, the tier is set to analytic, and the computation is cross-checked against an independent official figure wherever one exists. Where two official sources disagree, both are carried and neither is preferred.

conventions.mhzCounting: Indian official practice counts PAIRED (FDD) spectrum by the uplink quantity only: a 2x5 MHz block is recorded as 5 MHz. Unpaired (TDD) spectrum in 2300, 2500, 3300 MHz and 26 GHz is counted as the full quantity. Every MHz figure in this file follows the convention used by the source document, which is the Indian one throughout. Comparing a 2010 3G MHz figure with a 2022 26 GHz MHz figure is therefore NOT comparing like with like - see the caveat on auction-2022.
conventions.quantumVersusValue: Share sold by QUANTITY and share sold by VALUE are different statistics and diverge sharply. DoT's own comparison in the 2 March 2021 PIB release gives 2016 as 41 per cent by quantity and 12 per cent by value, and 2021 as 37 per cent by quantity and 19 per cent by value. This file's headline series is by quantity; the value share is recorded where an official source states it.
conventions.crore: 1 crore = 10 million. 1 lakh crore = 1 trillion rupees.

auctions.exactWording: 'The e-auction was conducted over 34 days (from 9th April, 2010 to 19th May, 2010) and involved 183 rounds of bidding across service areas. All the 71 blocks that were put up for auction across the 22 service areas in the country were sold, leaving no unsold lots.'
auctions.notes: THE 100 PER CENT SOLD SHARE IS DOT'S OWN WORDING AND IT IS ABOUT BLOCKS, NOT ABOUT DEMAND. The number of blocks was set circle by circle at three in seventeen service areas and four in five (Punjab, West Bengal, Himachal Pradesh, Bihar, Jammu & Kashmir), for 71 in total; 71 x 5 MHz = 355 MHz. The Rs 50,968.37 crore is the sum of the 71 winning prices in DoT's own result table and is the PRIVATE-OPERATOR total only. BSNL and MTNL were separately required to pay the auction-determined price for the 3G spectrum already assigned to them; that amount is NOT in this document and is recorded as a gap. The CAG's conclusion chapter states that 3G generated 'revenues of Rs 67,718.95 crore', which is Rs 16,750.58 crore more than the private-bidder total - consistent with the public-undertaking component, but the CAG report does not itself decompose the figure, so the decomposition is not asserted here. NINE COMPANIES APPLIED; the number that actually placed bids is not established by any document opened for this file. DoT's applicant list carries its own caveat: 'These lists are provided for information only and do not in any way imply that these Applications have been processed or pre-qualified.' Two applicants (Etisalat DB Telecom and Videocon Telecommunications) won nothing. || RESERVE PRICE AND TOTAL RAISED, from a Rajya Sabha answer of 19 August 2010: 'The total reserve price kept for spectrum auction was Rs. 14,330 crores for 3G services and Rs. 5,250 crores for BWA services. Total amount raised by the Government through spectrum auctions is Rs. 67,718.95 crores from 3G services and Rs. 38,542.11 crores from BWA services. This amount includes the share of MTNL/BSNL.' The 3G auction therefore realised 4.72 times its reserve price - the highest ratio of any auction in this file by a wide margin.

NO DOCUMENT OPENED FOR THIS FILE SAYS SO, so the reconciliation is an observation about the arithmetic, not a sourced fact. Both figures are carried. bandDetail.internalInconsistency: THE NIA CONTRADICTS ITSELF ON THIS FIGURE. Its prose says: 'In the case of the 800MHz Auction, the Government shall auction 3 blocks, each of 1.25MHz (paired) in each of the 19 Service Areas as per details given in Table 2-B below. In two Service Areas of Punjab and Andhra Pradesh, the Government shall auction 2 blocks, each of 1.25MHz (paired). No spectrum is being auctioned in the Service Area of Rajasthan.' That gives 19 x 3 + 2 x 2 = 61 blocks = 76.25 MHz. But Table 2-B on the facing page lists a FOURTH frequency spot in fifteen service areas, giving 76 spots = 95 MHz if every listed spot is a block. The document does not reconcile the two. The prose figure is used as primary because it is a count and the table is a frequency list; the alternative is carried. On the alternative, the 2012 auction's total offered quantum is 397.5 MHz and its sold share 31.76 per cent rather than 33.33 per cent.
bandDetail.note: NO PUBLIC REPORT FOR THE NOVEMBER 2012 800 MHz AUCTION WAS FOUND, and no DoT document opened for this file states in terms that the band drew no bids. auctions.reconciliation: THIS AUCTION IS THE ONE INDEPENDENTLY DOUBLE-CHECKED. TRAI's 2018 band tables give offered and sold band by band; adding them gives 770 + 73.75 + 9.4 + 221.6 + 360 + 320 + 600 = 2,354.75 MHz offered and 0 + 15 + 0 + 174.8 + 85 + 320 + 370 = 964.80 MHz sold, a sold share of 40.97 per cent. Separately, counting every frequency row in DoT's own 30-page frequency-assignment report and multiplying by the block size for each band (1.25 MHz in 800, 0.2 MHz in 1800, 5 MHz in 2100, 10 MHz unpaired in 2300 and 2500) gives 15.00 + 174.80 + 85.00 + 320.00 + 370.00 = 964.80 MHz - the SAME figure, band by band, from a different document by a different publisher. Multiplying each block by its service-area winning price in that same DoT report gives a total of Rs 65,789.12 crore. And DoT's own 2021 statement that 2016 sold '41% by quantity' matches 40.97 per cent. Three independent checks agree. A THIRD independent confirmation arrived from Parliament: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 6351, answered 12 April 2017 by the Minister of State for Communications, gives 2,354.75 MHz put to auction and 964.80 MHz sold - the same two numbers, from the Government's own answer on the floor of the House. The widely circulated 2,354.55 MHz was not found in any document opened for this file.
auctions.notes: The Rs 65,789.12 crore total and the seven per-operator rows are COMPUTED from DoT's frequency-assignment report, not published as totals in it; they are tiered analytic even though they reconcile to the MHz figures exactly. Reserve price total is NULL: no official statement of the aggregate value at reserve price for the 2016 auction was opened for this file, and the figures of roughly Rs 5.36 lakh crore or Rs 5.63 lakh crore that circulate were not sourced. Consequently the 12-per-cent-by-value figure is carried as DoT's own statement and not recomputed. Seven bidders is DoT's number and it matches the seven distinct winners in the frequency-assignment report - meaning every bidder won something, so no one bid and lost. THE 2016 UNSOLD SHARE IS DRIVEN ALMOST ENTIRELY BY TWO BANDS: 700 MHz alone accounts for 770 of the 1,389.95 unsold MHz, or 55 per cent of everything unsold, and 2100 MHz for another 275 MHz. Strip 700 MHz out and the sold share rises from 41 per cent to 60.9 per cent.

values.source: Computed from DoT's own October 2016 frequency-assignment public report by counting every frequency row and multiplying by that band's block size and that service area's winning price per block. The MHz side of the same computation reconciles exactly, band by band, with TRAI's independently published tables and with the Lok Sabha answer.

The same table's MHz-sold figure (964.8) and sold share (40.97 per cent) agree with this file's computation to the decimal, so the difference is in the money, not the quantity. Rs 980.00 crore happens to be the winning price per block for Karnataka in the 2300 MHz band in DoT's own frequency-assignment report - one block's worth. unsoldShareSeries.innocentReading: MANDATORY, AND IT SHIPS WITH THE NUMBER. A high unsold share is exactly what a reserve price set above what buyers will pay produces, and it is equally what a market with no unmet demand produces. Both readings fit every row of this series, and this file contains nothing that distinguishes them. Four specific facts should stop anyone treating this series as a scandal series. (1) THE REGULATOR ITSELF TREATED THE 2016 RESULT AS A PRICING PROBLEM AND CUT THE PRICE. The single band that accounts for 55 per cent of all spectrum unsold in 2016 is 700 MHz; in its recommendations of 1 August 2018 TRAI recommended 'that reserve price of 700 MHz band should be equal to 2 times of reserve price of 1800 MHz spectrum band' (paragraph 3.106), and recommended that 'in LSAs where spectrum was offered in October 2016 auction but remained entirely unsold, the reserve price should be lower of the figures - 80% of average valuation or the reserve price as fixed in October 2016 auction' (paragraph 3.59). A regulator lowering a reserve price after nobody bought is the mechanism working, not evidence of anything else. (2) In 2024, DoT gives an operational reason in the release itself - the 5G spectrum bought in 2022 was still being monetised - and an operator sitting on unused spectrum has no reason to buy more at any price. (3) TRAI records the change in the buyer side as a fact of industry structure, not of auction design: 'At the time of previous auctions on an average there were 8 to 10 TSPs ... in last two years the Telecom Industry has been undergoing consolidation phase ... With the result, now the no of TSPs is reduced to practically four' (paragraph 3.104). Fewer buyers with more spectrum already in hand produces a lower sold share at any reserve price. (4) The two auctions with a 100 per cent sold share, 2010 3G and 2010 BWA, achieved it because the number of blocks per circle was fixed at three or four in a market with seven to eleven interested parties; scarcity was designed in on the supply side. A sold share is a joint product of supply, reserve price and demand, and this file measures only one of the three.

biddersPerAuctionSeries.whatThisDoesAndDoesNotShow: The count falls from nine and eleven applicants in 2010 to three participants in 2021 and 2024. THIS FILE DOES NOT EXPLAIN WHY AND MAKES NO CLAIM ABOUT IT. Three things make the series harder to read than it looks. First, the units change: 2010 is applicants, 2012 and 2013 are winners, 2016 onward are participants, and these are not the same quantity - an applicant list is longer than a bidder list, which is at least as long as a winner list. Second, the eligible universe changed by operation of law and by corporate action outside any auction: the Supreme Court quashed 122 licences in 2012, and the sector consolidated through mergers and exits between 2016 and 2020. Third, in 2016 and every year after, every bidder won something, so the count of bidders equals the count of winners and carries no information about competitive tension within a lot. The one auction where a bidder count would be most informative - how many parties competed for the SAME block - is not published for any Indian spectrum auction in any document opened for this file.

twoGRecord.claim: In 2008 the Department of Telecommunications issued Unified Access Service licences with 2G spectrum bundled in, at an entry fee discovered by bidding in 2001, under a first-come-first-served procedure whose cut-off date was moved backwards from 1 October 2007 to 25 September 2007 and whose priority rule was changed on the day the Letters of Intent were issued.

twoGRecord.exactWording: On the cut-off date (Executive Summary, item (vi), citing paragraphs 4.1.2 and 4.6): 'The TRAI report of August 2007 had recommended "no cap" on the number of licences in any service area. Despite this recommendation of TRAI, the DoT issued a Press Release on 24th September 2007 stating that applications for issue of licences would be accepted only upto 1.10.2007. This action, in effect, conveyed fixation of an artificial cap in the number of licenses to be awarded. ... To further compound the earlier decision, of restricting consideration of applications received up to 1.10.2007, the DoT further advanced this date to restrict issuance of Letters of Intent (LoIs) only to applications received up to 25.09.2007. This was ostensibly to avoid legal implications in view of the shortage of spectrum for GSM services.' || On first-come-first-served (item (vii), paragraph 4.6): 'However, audit found that DoT deviated even from the FCFS policy in letter and spirit. The applications submitted between March 2006 and 25th September 2007 were issued the LoIs simultaneously on a single day, viz. 10th January 2008. A notice was issued through a press release giving less than an hour to collect the same. This decision to issue LoIs simultaneously to all applicants was taken at the level of the Minister. ... By changing the FCFS criteria, some licensees, who could proactively anticipate such procedural changes were ready with the Demand Drafts drawn on dates prior to the notification of cut off date by DoT and could avail the benefit of first right to allocation of spectrum, having jumped the queue.' || On the changed priority rule (paragraph 4.6, body): 'On 10 January 2008 afternoon, the DoT through the Press Information Bureau informed that all eligible applicants who applied for UAS licences up to 25 September 2007 would be issued LoIs. It was also mentioned in the press release that the DoT has been implementing a policy of FCFS for the grant of UAS licences under which initially an application which is received first will be processed first and thereafter if found eligible will be granted LoI and then who so ever, complies with the condition of LoIs first will be granted UAS licence. This stipulation introduced for the first time by the DoT took away the relevance of the date of application and grossly violated the sanctity and transparency of the FCFS policy being followed hitherto by the DoT.' || On the Telecom Commission (paragraph 4.5, body): 'This is further corroborated by the fact that the date of the meeting of Telecom Commission which was scheduled to discuss the issues relating to issue of pending applications for licence and pricing of spectrum was postponed from 9 January 2008 to 15 January 2008. Without Telecom Commission getting an opportunity to discuss the matter, 121 LoIs were issued on 10 January 2008.'

twoGRecord.notes: THE DATE TEST APPLIED FORWARD RATHER THAN BACKWARD. Everything in this record is a date, and the dates are what carry the finding: a press release on 24 September 2007 fixing a cut-off of 1 October; a decision to move that cut-off BACKWARDS to 25 September, the day a newspaper report of the cut-off appeared; a Telecom Commission meeting on pricing postponed from 9 to 15 January 2008; and Letters of Intent issued on 10 January 2008, in the six-day gap that postponement created. None of that is an allegation. It is a sequence, and every element of it is in a tabled audit report. WHAT IT DOES NOT ESTABLISH is that any particular person acted corruptly, or that any particular company knew the sequence in advance. The CAG's own language on the last point is careful and conditional - 'some licensees, who COULD PROACTIVELY ANTICIPATE such procedural changes' - and it names no one.

twoGRecord.claim: THE CAG PUBLISHED A RANGE OF FOUR ESTIMATES, NOT A LOSS FIGURE. Its Report No. 19 of 2010 sets out four different bases for valuing the 2G spectrum given away in 2007-08 and prints all four side by side: Rs 57,666 crore, Rs 67,364 crore, Rs 69,626 crore and Rs 1,76,645 crore. The Rs 1.76 lakh crore that entered public circulation is the HIGHEST of the four and rests on one specific assumption - that 2G spectrum in 2008 was worth what 3G spectrum fetched at auction in 2010. THIS IS AN ESTIMATE THE CAG PUBLISHED. IT IS NOT A FINDING THAT A LOSS OF THAT SIZE OCCURRED, AND THE REPORT SAYS SO IN TERMS.

twoGRecord.notes: WHY THE RANGE MATTERS MORE THAN THE HEADLINE. The four estimates differ by a factor of three. They differ because they answer four different questions: what one bidder said it would pay, what a different band fetched two years later, and what two foreign investors paid for equity in two specific companies. A range of Rs 57,666 crore to Rs 1,76,645 crore is not a measurement with an error bar; it is four incompatible valuations printed together because the auditor could not choose between them and said so. Reporting only the top of the range is not rounding - it is selecting the single most aggressive assumption and dropping the report's own warning about it. This file therefore never uses the phrase 'the 1.76 lakh crore loss' and never prints the figure without the other three.

reservePriceTotalsEstablished.note: Only four of the ten auctions have an official aggregate reserve valuation in any document opened for this file: 2010 3G (Rs 14,330 crore), 2010 BWA (Rs 5,250 crore), 2021 (Rs 3,92,332.70 crore for 2,251.25 MHz) and 2024 (Rs 96,238.45 crore). The ratio of money realised to reserve valuation - arguably a sharper test of an aggressive reserve price than the unsold share - can therefore be computed for four auctions only: 2010 3G 472 per cent, 2010 BWA 734 per cent, 2021 19.8 per cent, 2024 11.8 per cent.

baseRates.reading: NON-DISCRIMINATING. At six of six, a band drawing no bid is the NORMAL outcome of an Indian multi-band spectrum auction, not an exceptional one, and 'band X went unsold' therefore proves nothing on its own about band X, its reserve price, or the auction. Anyone treating an empty band as evidence of failure has to explain why the same thing happened in every auction including the two the government treats as its most successful.

baseRates.reading: WEAK, AND WEAKENING TO USELESS. Across all seven auctions with a bidder count, 32 of 34 bidders won something. Exactly TWO documented bidders in the whole file bid and won nothing: Tata Teleservices Limited in February 2014 and Telewings Communications Services in March 2015. From 2016 onward the rate is 17 of 17 - every bidder won. The published participation count therefore contains almost no information about losing, and cannot be used as a measure of competitive tension. What would measure tension - how many bidders competed for the SAME block in the same service area - is not published for any Indian spectrum auction in any document opened for this file. THE ABSENCE IS THE POINT.

baseRates.reading: PUBLISH BOTH OR NEITHER, AND PUBLISH THE SPREAD. The eight sold shares from 2012 to 2024 run from 1.34 per cent to 88.85 per cent; their simple mean is 48.4 per cent and it describes no actual auction. The pooled figure over the auctions with an MHz denominator is 61.0 per cent and is dominated entirely by the 2022 auction's 62,700 MHz of 26 GHz millimetre wave. Any single 'average unsold share for Indian spectrum' is a choice about how to weight a band that did not exist in the auction programme before 2022 and whose price per MHz is roughly one four-hundredth of the 700 MHz band's. This file's series is per auction for that reason and no cross-auction average is offered as a finding.

baseRates.reading: THE STATISTIC THE UNSOLD-SHARE SERIES CANNOT SEE. In 2010 the government set a reserve price and the market paid between five and seven times it. In 2021 and 2024 the government set reserve prices totalling Rs 3.92 lakh crore and Rs 96,238 crore and the market paid a fifth and an eighth of them. A reserve price that is repeatedly cleared many times over is one set below the market; a reserve price that is repeatedly under-cleared is one set above it. That is the whole innocent reading of the unsold-share series in four numbers - and it can only be computed for four of ten auctions, because the reserve valuation is not published for the other six. NOTE the confound: the 2010 auctions offered scarce single-band spectrum to seven to eleven contenders, and the 2021 and 2024 auctions offered everything the government held to three. Supply, reserve price and the number of buyers all moved together, and none of the four ratios isolates any of them.

gaps: NO SINGLE OFFICIAL TABLE COVERS 2010-2024. The nearest thing is DoT's own WPC Wing paper 'A short Analysis of Spectrum auction in India' by V. J. Christopher, Senior Deputy Wireless Adviser, which tabulates six auctions from 2010 to 2016 and stops there. It is hosted on the DoT website but it is an officer-authored study, not a statutory return, and it disagrees with other DoT documents on four separate figures. Nothing covering 2010 to 2024 in one place was found. DoT Annual Reports for 2013-14 through 2016-17 could not be retrieved at all - the live paths 404 and the current site serves no server-rendered content - and remain the single most promising missing document.

RESERVE PRICE TOTALS ARE MISSING FOR SIX OF TEN AUCTIONS. Established: 2010 3G (Rs 14,330 crore) and 2010 BWA (Rs 5,250 crore) from Rajya Sabha Question No. 2750 of 19 August 2010; 2021 (Rs 3,92,332.70 crore) from the Cabinet release; 2024 (Rs 96,238.45 crore) from PIB. NOT established: 2012, 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016 and 2022. The figures of roughly Rs 5.36 lakh crore or Rs 5.63 lakh crore for 2016 and Rs 4.3 lakh crore for 2022 circulate widely and were not sourced. Because of this, the realisation-to-reserve ratio can be computed for four auctions only.

THE OFFERED QUANTUM IS MISSING FOR 2013, 2014 AND 2015 even though their SOLD SHARES are published. DoT's WPC table gives percentages sold without an offered-MHz column, and no NIA total was opened. Dividing sold by share implies roughly 195 MHz (2013), 431 MHz (2014) and 471 MHz (2015), but those are arithmetic on a rounded percentage and are not asserted. For 2015, three of the four bands have published quantities - 103.75 + 177.8 + 99.2 = 380.75 MHz - and the fourth, 2100 MHz, was never announced in any document opened here.

FOUR UNRESOLVED CONFLICTS BETWEEN OFFICIAL SOURCES, all carried in full on the auction records: (1) 2010 MHz sold - 355 and 880 MHz counted from DoT's result notes against 465 and 1,320 MHz in DoT's WPC analysis, the difference in each case being exactly one block per service area. (2) 2012 - 126.25 MHz and Rs 9,407.64 crore counted from DoT result documents against 127.5 MHz and Rs 9,642.11 crore in the WPC analysis. (3) 2013 - Rs 3,639.48 crore computed from DoT's own corrected result annexure against Rs 4,113.65 crore in the WPC analysis, for an auction with one bidder. (4) 2015 - Rs 1,09,874 crore announced by PIB as provisional on the closing day against Rs 1,13,932.2 crore in the WPC analysis. Also: 2016 - Rs 65,789.12 crore computed from DoT's frequency-assignment report against Rs 64,809.12 crore in the WPC analysis, a gap of exactly Rs 980 crore. None of these is resolved by any document opened for this file.

THE BSNL AND MTNL COMPONENT OF THE 2010 AUCTIONS IS NOT SEPARATELY PUBLISHED. The Rajya Sabha answer of 19 August 2010 gives combined totals of Rs 67,718.95 crore (3G) and Rs 38,542.11 crore (BWA) and says in terms 'This amount includes the share of MTNL/BSNL', but does not break it out. DoT's WPC analysis states the private-bidder figures with the remark 'Revenue from BSNL/MTNL not taken into a/c'. Subtracting gives Rs 16,750.58 crore for 3G and Rs 12,846.57 crore for BWA, but that is arithmetic across two documents and the BWA remainder does not match the Rs 12,847.77 crore that circulates. Recorded as not established.

THE NUMBER OF OPERATORS THAT ACTUALLY BID IS UNKNOWN FOR 2010 AND 2012. For 2010 only DoT's applicant list exists (9 for 3G, 11 for BWA), and it carries its own disclaimer that publication 'does not in any way imply that these Applications have been processed or pre-qualified'. For 2012 only the five successful bidders can be counted. This is the weakest part of the bidders-per-auction series and it is weakest at exactly the end of the series where participation was highest.

NO INDIAN SPECTRUM AUCTION PUBLISHES BIDDERS PER LOT. The statistic that would measure competitive tension - how many bidders contested the same block in the same service area - is not published for any auction in this file. DoT's daily public reports publish 'Aggregate Demand' and 'Excess Demand' per service area per band per round, which count BLOCKS demanded, not bidders demanding them. A bidder count that can barely fall below the winner count, plus a demand series that counts blocks, means the participation data in this domain cannot distinguish a contested auction from an uncontested one.

THE 2022 AUCTION'S 600 MHz AND 2300 MHz QUANTITIES ARE MISSING. The Cabinet release names ten bands; the result release's two tables have eight columns each and their band figures fall 721 MHz short of the stated 72,098 MHz total. Neither release states how much 600 MHz or 2300 MHz spectrum was offered. The 2022 sold share is therefore computed against a total whose composition is not fully published.

THE 2022 AUCTION'S ROUND COUNT AND EXACT DATES ARE MISSING. Neither the result release nor the Year End Review gives a round count, and the two official statements on timing disagree - the Year End Review says the auction was 'held in July 2022' while the result release is dated 2 August 2022. Round counts are established for every other auction in the file: 183, 117, 14, 3, 68, 115, 31, 6 and 7.

THE 2012 800 MHz RESULT IS INFERRED, NOT PUBLISHED. No public report for the November 2012 800 MHz auction was found. The zero rests on the absence of any CDMA operator from DoT's list of five successful bidders and on DoT's own reference, five months later, to 'the March, 2013 800MHz band spectrum auction'. If a November 2012 800 MHz result document exists showing any sale, the 2012 sold share moves.

THE 2012 NIA CONTRADICTS ITSELF ON THE 800 MHz QUANTUM and neither figure is a published total: its prose gives 61 blocks (76.25 MHz), its Table 2-B lists 76 frequency spots (95 MHz). Both are carried and the 2012 sold share is given on the prose figure.

THE 2016 WINNING-BID TOTAL AND PER-OPERATOR SPLIT ARE COMPUTED, NOT PUBLISHED. Rs 65,789.12 crore and the seven operator rows are derived by counting every frequency row in DoT's 30-page frequency-assignment report and multiplying by that band's block size and that service area's winning price per block. The MHz side of that computation reconciles exactly with TRAI's independently published 2016 tables and with the Lok Sabha answer of 12 April 2017 - but DoT never printed the money total itself in any document opened here, and its own WPC paper gives a figure Rs 980 crore lower.

PER-OPERATOR ALLOCATIONS ARE MISSING FOR 2013 AND 2015. For 2013 the single winner absorbs everything so the gap is formal. For 2015 the DoT result report gives per-service-area winning prices and which company received which frequency, but no operator-level rollup of the kind published for 2014 - so no MHz or rupee figure per operator is recorded for the largest auction in the file by value.

THE 2016 12-PER-CENT-BY-VALUE FIGURE CANNOT BE CROSS-CHECKED. DoT's statement that 2016 sold '12% by value' implies a reserve valuation of roughly Rs 5.5 lakh crore against the money realised, but no official aggregate reserve figure for 2016 was opened, so the 12 per cent is carried as DoT's assertion and is not recomputed.

DOT'S CURRENT WEBSITE CANNOT BE BROWSED FOR THESE DOCUMENTS. dot.gov.in is a client-rendered Next.js application whose pages return an empty HTML shell to any non-JavaScript client, and no public API endpoint for its content was found in its JavaScript bundles. Every DoT document in this file was reached either through its /static/uploads/ path, discovered via domain-restricted search, or through the Internet Archive. There is no way to enumerate what else DoT holds, so the absence of a document from this file is not evidence that DoT has not published it.

SPECTRUM ACQUIRED OUTSIDE AUCTION IS NOT IN THIS FILE AT ALL. Spectrum trading and sharing, permitted since 2015, moved substantial holdings between operators without any auction; TRAI's paragraph 3.104 records that the secondary market 'increased the spectrum availability with existing leading TSPs manifold'. A register of auctions therefore understates how much spectrum changed hands, and a falling sold share in auctions is not the same statistic as falling demand for spectrum.

THE 21 DECEMBER 2017 TRIAL-COURT JUDGMENTS COULD NOT BE OPENED ON AN OFFICIAL COURT SERVER. Both were read from Internet Archive captures of a third-party judgment database (indiankanoon.org), which is now behind a Cloudflare challenge that this environment cannot pass. Delhi district-court hosts under dcourts.gov.in did not resolve; services.ecourts.gov.in is behind a session-bound image captcha; judgments.ecourts.gov.in covers the Supreme Court and High Courts only, not district courts. Every case-management fact in those captures is independently corroborated by the Delhi High Court's own judgment of 22 March 2024, which WAS read from delhihighcourt.nic.in - but the quoted passages themselves rest on a mirror, and the record says so.

THE ESSAR / LOOP TRIAL-COURT JUDGMENT OF 21 DECEMBER 2017 IS NOT IN THIS FILE. A third acquittal was delivered the same day in the connected Essar/Loop case, and the Delhi High Court record shows CBI filed a third leave petition against it (CRL.L.P. 257/2018). No copy of that judgment could be opened - the Internet Archive has no capture of it - so nothing about its case number, accused or reasoning is asserted here.

rejected.candidate: Describing the CAG's Rs 1,76,645 crore as 'the 2G loss' or 'the loss to the exchequer'
rejected.reason: The report calls it presumptive, prints three other totals beside it ranging down to Rs 57,666 crore, says its assumptions 'could be open to questions and be disputed', and says the amount of loss 'could be debated'. A fifth of the Rs 1.76 lakh crore is not about the 122 licences at all but about spectrum given to thirteen incumbent operators beyond their contracted 6.2 MHz. And in December 2017 a court acquitted every accused in the criminal case built on those transactions. The figure is carried in this file only as one of four published estimates, always with the other three.

rejected.candidate: Treating the 2024 auction's '26.5 per cent sold' as comparable with 2016's 41 per cent or 2021's 37 per cent
rejected.reason: The 26.5 per cent uses a denominator - 533.6 MHz - that is the spectrum in the four bands that turned out to draw bids, identified after the auction closed. Measured against the 10,522.35 MHz DoT said it was auctioning the day before, the figure is 1.34 per cent. A denominator chosen after the result cannot be compared across years. Both figures are carried on the auction record and the series uses the ex ante one.

rejected.candidate: Ranking the 2022 auction as the most successful because 71 per cent of the spectrum sold
rejected.reason: 87 per cent of the 72,098 MHz offered was 26 GHz millimetre wave, a band never previously auctioned in India, and 88 per cent of the spectrum sold was 26 GHz and 3300 MHz. In the traditional sub-3 GHz bands with published columns, 396.2 of 1,417 MHz sold - 27.96 per cent, worse than 2016 or 2021. The 71 per cent is a units artefact of counting millimetre-wave MHz alongside 700 MHz MHz.

rejected.candidate: A pooled 'average unsold share for Indian spectrum auctions'
rejected.reason: The unweighted mean of the four post-2016 sold shares is 37.6 per cent and the pooled figure is 61.0 per cent, from the same four auctions. Any single number is a choice about how to weight the 2022 mmWave band. Both are published in baseRates and neither is offered as a finding.

rejected.candidate: A claim that competition in Indian spectrum auctions collapsed after the 2012 cancellation of 122 licences
rejected.reason: Unfalsifiable on the available record and confounded at every step. There is no bidder-participation count for 2012, 2013, 2014 or 2015, so the years immediately after the cancellation are exactly the years with no data. TRAI's own explanation for the fall in operator numbers, published in 2018, names merger and the secondary trading market, not the 2012 judgment. And every bidder in every auction since 2016 won something, so the count cannot detect competition anyway.

rejected.candidate: Reading a high unsold share as evidence of a rigged or failed auction
rejected.reason: A reserve price above buyers' valuations produces exactly this pattern, and so does a market with no unmet demand. TRAI itself responded to the 2016 result by recommending a lower reserve price for 700 MHz and by recommending that where spectrum offered in 2016 remained entirely unsold the reserve should be capped at the 2016 price. That is the mechanism correcting itself. The innocent reading ships attached to the series.

rejected.candidate: The figures of Rs 5.36 lakh crore or Rs 5.63 lakh crore as the 2016 reserve valuation, and Rs 4.3 lakh crore for 2022
rejected.reason: Widely circulated and not sourced. No official statement of either aggregate was opened for this file. Recorded as a gap rather than carried.

rejected.candidate: The claim that spectrum auctions were held every year from 2010 except 2015
rejected.reason: Contradicted by DoT's own daily public report headed 'Spectrum Auction in 2100, 1800, 900 & 800MHz Bands - Daily Public Report: End of day 18, Date 2015-03-21'. There was an auction in 2015 and it ran at least 18 days and 97 rounds. There was no auction in 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2023 or 2025.

rejected.candidate: Using the auction ordinal ('the 8th auction', 'the 10th auction') as an identifier
rejected.reason: DoT calls the July 2022 auction 'the 8th Spectrum Auction', which requires counting the 2010 3G and BWA auctions as one event; press accounts calling the 2024 auction 'the 10th' count them as two and count differently again. The ordinal is ambiguous by at least one and is recorded only where an official source uses it.
